newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bullish T-bonds to jump from 109-21 prop.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bullish T-bonds to jump from 109-21 prop.

text.p: June T-bond futures remain in bullish mood on both a technical and a fundamental basis, and any dips provide an opportunity for buying, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
"The economy is balancing the budget deficit, technically the market is behaving and the three and 10-year auctions should help," said Bill Westgate, vice president at HSBC Securities.
Hourly trendline support at 109-21 will help the contract, said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in a note to clients.
June T-bonds were at 110-01 at 1038 GMT in automated trade, unchanged from Monday's Chicago settlement price.
"We use pullbacks as a buying opporutnity, looking for attempts to clear the upper limits of the downtrend channel at 111-18," said HSBC Futures in a research note.
T-bonds have held a positive tone since the Clinton administration and congressional Republicans agreed on Friday to balance the budget by 2002, analysts said.
The U.S. Treasury will sell three-year notes on Tuesday and 10-year notes on Wednesday.
"This will provide an opportunity for those who haven't already to get long," said Westgate.
"We have seen very good buying," he added.
In the longer term, "our next objective is to get out of this downtrend that we have been in since early December," said Westgate.
The June contract reached a high of 116-00 on December 3.
"If we can break that we can see significant further gains," said Westgate.
September Eurodollar futures were at 93.870 in automated trade, 0.015 below Monday's settlement price.
